r0.why: Variation of properties in solid Earth [1]; layers at increasing depth, naming depends on approach [11],[12]; mechanical vs chemical [2],[3],[13]; partial alignment, names not mixed [14].

r1.why: Mechanical layers [2]; silicate crust, iron-magnesium silicate mantle, iron-nickel core [3],[13],[30]; flowing upper core makes the magnetic field [3].

r2.why: Mass from gravity or satellites [6],[7]; 6x10^24 kg [9]; density via pendulum gravimetry, 5.515 g/cm3 [8],[10].

r3.why: 'Its base, the Mohorovicic discontinuity or Moho' is not supported: the cited sentences [22],[23] describe the Moho as a seismic velocity change but none says it is the base of the crust (the crust-mantle boundary is in uncited [21]).

r4.why: 2,890 km, thickest [26]; solid but flows [31]; convection drives plates [32]; radioactive and formation heat [33]; pressure reduces flow [34]; viscosity range and water comparison [35],[36].

r5.why: Outer core fluid, 2,260 km, iron-nickel, below mantle [37]; top at 2,890 km [38]; transition 5,150 km [39]; solid ball 1,220 km, 70% of Moon radius [41]; Lehmann 1936 [42]; shear waves [43].
